MARKET.head: Liv-ex brings LWIN matching and price data into one List Studio workflow
MARKET.summ: Liv-ex has introduced two connected improvements designed to help members work with wine lists more efficiently and at scale
takeaways: Liv-ex has added its member-exclusive Wine Matcher to List Studio, letting members match wine lists to LWIN and enrich them in bulk.
The redesigned matching engine, combining modern AI with Liv-ex's proprietary data, reports precision above 99% and processes up to 1,500 lines per minute.
Lists of up to 10,000 lines can now be enriched with Liv-ex market price, last trade, best bid and offer, critic scores and ABVs.

MARKET.head: VINITECH-SIFEL 2026 trade show set for Bordeaux, 1-3 December
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL runs 1-3 December 2026 in Bordeaux, with 700 exhibitors and 40,000 professionals from 70 countries.
The International Buyers Program offers eligible overseas buyers with equipment investment plans 4-star hotel stays and travel support.
Free technical estate visits for international professionals are organised by Interco Nouvelle-Aquitaine from 30 November.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA moves to New York with 300 exhibitors in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, debuts in New York City at Pier 36 on October 26 and 27, 2026.
After two years in Chicago, the event will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, its largest exhibitor count to date.
Regional collectives from Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lazio and Sardinia join a 95-winery delegation organized by the Italian Trade Agency.

MARKET.head: Global wine demand shifts from red toward white and sparkling styles
MARKET.summ: The global wine industry has been undergoing a significant structural transformation. While declining overall wine consumption has attracted considerable attention, another important trend has emerged beneath the surface: a steady shift in consumer demand from red wine towards white and sparkling wine.
takeaways: IWSR data shows red wine's share of global wine consumption fell from about 52 per cent in 2012 to 43 per cent in 2025.
Over the same period white wine rose from 31 to 34 per cent and sparkling wine from 8 to 13 per cent.
Overall wine consumption has declined since the late 2010s, with white and sparkling proving more resilient than red.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US AVAs bid for recognition, from California to New Jersey
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed American Viticultural Areas are in early stages awaiting Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau approval, which can take years.
Proposed Annapolis-Sea Ranch AVA in Sonoma County would cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres of grapes across a dozen vineyards.
Proposed Deschutes River AVA in central Oregon would be the state's first recognized winegrowing region, spanning 723,760 acres.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup flags Uncle Nearest sale talks and other drinks news
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Uncle Nearest’s potential buyers, Mark Zuckerberg’s Guinness flop, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: The roundup also covers Southern Glazer's bribery snafu and OpenTable's 2026 restaurant report.
Pop-Tarts reportedly exited its BuzzBallz collaboration, and a Trump ban on Canadian alcohol is noted.

CULTURE.head: China hosts OIV World Congress in Yinchuan, first time in Asia
CULTURE.summ: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine, marking a historic first for Asia
takeaways: The 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine was held in Yinchuan, Ningxia, from 12 to 16 October 2026.
It was the first OIV World Congress ever held in Asia, hosted by China.
More than 600 participants from 47 countries attended, along with 420 scientific contributions and six technical visits.

CULTURE.head: Next Wave Awards AAPI Food & Wine Nonprofit of the Year Honor
CULTURE.summ: In 2020, Lois and Dave Cho became the first Korean American winemakers in Oregon when they launched CHO Wines in the Willamette Valley. The fast-growing winery quickly amassed a following and received critical acclaim, but they kept fielding the same question: “What informs your palate for wine?” The answer to that question...
takeaways: AAPI Food & Wine, a nonprofit run by Lois and Dave Cho of CHO Wines, was named Next Wave Awards Nonprofit of the Year.
The festival launched in 2023 in Oregon with 12 Portland chefs and five AAPI-owned Willamette Valley wineries, selling out 1,000 tickets.
The nonprofit has since held three annual Oregon festivals and expanded to New York City with a three-day celebration this year.

CULTURE.head: Cloudy and unfiltered wines gain ground, led by pét nat and M&S rosé
CULTURE.summ:
There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection …

Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth - that there is nothing new under the sun - certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural...
takeaways: Marks & Spencer's Trouble organic rosé is the first cloudy still wine sold in a British supermarket.
Cloudy pét nats are bottled before fermentation finishes and are typically not disgorged, leaving sediment that makes them hazy.
Ottolenghi's Zainab Majerikova says cloudy house wines add texture and suit big, complex-flavoured food.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American drinkers abroad are curious, though vodka and Martinis persist
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: European bartenders at London's Connaught Bar and Madrid's Rosewood Villa Magna say American visitors are curious, open and engaged.
Americans still request vodka Martinis, spirit swaps and American cocktails, though many now ask bartenders for local recommendations.
Americans took a record 24 million trips to Europe in 2025, a figure expected to rise another 5 percent this year.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian São Francisco Valley reds keep polyphenols high through 12-month storage
SCIENCE.summ: Young varietal and experimental wines from Vitis vinifera - Petit Verdot, Tempranillo, and Syrah - cultivated in a tropical semiarid region (Northeast Brazil) were evaluated with regard to their phenolic composition and chromatic characteristics during a storage period of 12-month
takeaways: Researchers from Brazilian universities and Embrapa tested young tropical wines from Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah grown in Northeast Brazil's semiarid São Francisco Valley.
Over 12 months of bottle storage, the wines' polyphenol levels fell as expected but stayed above published levels, such as anthocyanins in Petit Verdot and trans-resveratrol in Syrah.
Petit Verdot showed less colour change than wines from temperate climates, and a separate sensory study found red wines softened over storage while whites stayed refreshing.

SCIENCE.head: Heat tents show grapevine fruit set responds differently by cultivar
SCIENCE.summ: In the 2009/2010 growing season undervine tents (a passive, open system) were used to increase daytime temperature by 3-5 oC over ambient during the growing season. Four grapevine cultivars (Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Semillon and Shiraz) were assessed for reproductive performance under these conditions
takeaways: Adelaide researchers used passive undervine tents in 2009/2010 to raise daytime temperatures 3-5 degrees C.
Chardonnay under heat had lower fruit set, fewer berries and lighter bunches, with reduced pollen tube growth.
Semillon and Shiraz showed higher fruit set and more pollen tubes entering the ovary under heat.

SCIENCE.head: Study tracks root growth of three rootstocks under two water regimes in rhizotrons
SCIENCE.summ: Grapevine is a landscape forming crop which, due to the quality and taste demanded by consumers, as well as the different agronomical practices, could be vulnerable to global change effects
takeaways: Researchers grew Grenache grafted onto 110 Richter, 41-B and 161-49 rootstocks in rhizotrons under two water regimes.
Roots grew most in summer during berry growth and ripening, and more roots formed under the higher water dose.
110 Richter developed higher root length than the other two rootstocks, though this did not raise vegetative growth.

SCIENCE.head: Part Two of vineyard lab series examines how irrigation water shapes soil minerals
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Nearly pure water, below 0.2 to 0.5 dS/m, strips minerals from soils and makes them more acidic and less fertile.
Well waters can carry macronutrients or micronutrients, while salinity and high sodium can damage vines and soils.

SCIENCE.head: Cover crops and mulching boost vineyard soil microbes and resilience, new studies find
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: A 2026 Environmental Microbiome study in non-irrigated northern Italian vineyards found cover-crop under-vine mulching raised microbial diversity.
The same study reported improved soil conditions and reduced pathogen pressure under the mulched inter-row system.
A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved soil cover, vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization.

SCIENCE.head: French wine harvest set to fall 14% below recent average after heat
SCIENCE.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: France's 2026 harvest is estimated at about 35 million hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
Champagne harvested early for the first time in September, with output down by half on last year and the five-year average.
Burgundy and Beaujolais output is projected at 30% below the five-year average, while Bordeaux is expected up 10% on 2025.

SCIENCE.head: SFI 2026 offers UK vineyards payments for cover crops and habitat actions
SCIENCE.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: The 2026 Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) includes vines and horticultural permanent crops, with 71 actions, several relevant to vineyards.
Vineyard cover crops such as overwinter cover (CSAM2) should ideally be sown by late August or early September to establish before winter.
The Rural Payments Agency uses satellite imagery to monitor SFI action delivery, and small-seeded cover mixes need a well-prepared, weed-free seedbed.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Santuvario, a natural wine producer in Alto Piemonte, Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Santuvario is a small natural wine producer based in the town of Borgomanero in Alto Piemonte, at the foot of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Santuvario is a small natural wine producer in Borgomanero, Alto Piemonte, run by Ivano Barbaglia and Paola Fornara since 2012.
Tasted at VinNatur Paris in November 2025, Santuvario's Gino Bianco 2022 (Erbaluce) scored 93/100 and Lazio 2022 (80% Nebbiolo, 20% Vespolina) scored 94/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Images: The Altar
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A mysterious artifact behind the winery at Mateus Nicolau de Almeida in the Douro Superior region, with a hillside of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Vinography's image post features an unexplained artifact behind the winery at Mateus Nicolau de Almeida in Portugal's Douro Superior region.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Pairing Wine With Fall
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Wines to pour with autumnal fare, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says fall cuisine in northern New England is earthy, rich, spiced, hearty and warm, with flavors darker than summer's.
Maker writes that autumnal foods are typically cooked, cured, pickled, smoked or dried, transforming them from their original state.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A Level Playing Field
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What do we mean by the word “Burgundian”? Used indiscriminately to describe a region that is famously, almost defiantly complex, it’s a term that covers so many appellations, terroirs and styles as to be almost meaningless, especially when it comes to white Burgundy. Are we talking Chablis, the Côte Beaune or the Mâconnais?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin ran a blind tasting of 24 Chardonnays, 14 from Burgundy and 10 from Pyramid Valley and Smith & Sheth in New Zealand, judged by 43 tasters.
Atkin scored three of five correct on the first two flights, five of seven on the third, and four of seven on the fourth when identifying Burgundies.
The 2024 Smith & Sheth Onewa Chardonnay from Gimblett Gravels, Hawkes Bay, narrowly lost to the 2023 Domaine Guffens-Heynen Saint Véran Clos de Poncetys.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From Livermore to the Loire: Cabernet Franc in Food & Wine, Robb Report, Le Point, JancisRobinson.com, and more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Food & Wine reports California has only 3,501 acres of Cabernet Franc in 2025, versus 90,040 acres of Cabernet Sauvignon, per the California Grape Acreage Report.
In February 2025, Livermore Valley officially named Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc as its signature red and white varieties.
Le Point's wine issue profiles Bourgueil, the only dedicated Cabernet Franc appellation featured, with critic Jacques Dupont tasting 50 wines blind.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya, has revised its bylaws to add certification for vi brisat, its orange-style wine.
Montsant's revised bylaws also add a classification for 'minimal intervention' wines requiring hand-harvesting, organic certification, and spontaneous fermentation.
The author says Montsant has about 15% fewer vineyard hectares than DOQ Priorat, but produces slightly more wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Most Burgundy Wine Buyers Are Still Shopping Backwards in 2026. Here’s the Strategy Négociants Hope You Never Learn
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Learn the strategy Burgundy wine négociants hope you never discover to find the best winery deals in 2026
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy négociant houses Louis Latour, Louis Jadot, Maison Albert Bichot and Bouchard Père & Fils dominate worldwide sales of Burgundy wine.
It cites Capitain-Gagnerot Corton-Charlemagne as a cheaper alternative to Coche-Dury, and Domaine Jean Féry Puligny-Montrachet as an alternative to Leflaive Clavoillon.

NEWSLETTERS.head: “Unquestionably Among the Greatest Wines in the World” (Tasting the 2024 Port Vintage)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: You’ll find no shortage of Vintage Port coverage on these virtual pages (something that, as I taste more and more vintages of the stuff, has become a source of amusing vexation as I search for whether or not a VP that I want to feature here has already been reviewed and featured here…). And you’ll […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude reviews the 2024 Vintage Port, with the headline calling it unquestionably among the greatest wines in the world.
The author notes frequent prior Vintage Port coverage on the site, which complicated checking whether a given port had already been featured.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A 1350 trade contract between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, held in Florence's State Archives.
A 2024 document unveiled by the Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano shows the term 'Vino Nobile' was used by the Jesuit order in 1766, predating the previously known 1787 usage.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and requested 400 bottles annually in a letter the following April.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine publishes 8 October in the UK and 10 November in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference by acknowledged experts, not too academic.
The book has 28 contributors, including Jane Anson on Bordeaux and Wink Lorch on the Jura, and rivals The Oxford Companion to Wine and The World Atlas of Wine.
